Contents
The Chief Executive’s Report for South Dublin County Council is 
presented to elected members at each monthly Council meeting.  
Section 136(2) of the Local Government Act 2001, as inserted by 
Section 51 of the Local Government Reform Act 2014, requires 
the Chief Executive to prepare a management report in relation to 
the performance of executive functions, including implementation 
of policy or other matters required by the Council in the exercise 
of its reserved functions, and the provision of services.  It should 
be viewed in conjunction with the various updates provided to Area 
Committee Meetings as well as the quarterly Capital Progress 
Report to full Council as part of the reporting structures to 
assist the elected members with their governance and oversight 
responsibilities.
The report includes important updates and information from 
across our various directorates and departments together with a 
range of key statistics that were developed in conjunction with the 
elected members.  It provides the opportunity to highlight major 
news events and to focus on different areas of our work that may 
not always get the attention it deserves while a selection of images 
from recent events is also included.

Airton Road Extension 
Opens
Two new safe route to school 
projects were officially opened 
last month delivering safety 
upgrades and supporting active 
travel at Scoil Maelruain and St 
Dominic’s National School, both 
in Old Bawn, Tallaght
At Scoil Maelruain, a new school 
street has been introduced on 
Old Bawn Avenue which includes 
restricted vehicle access at 
the cul-de-sac, raised zebra 
crossings, resurfaced footpaths, 
pencil-style bollards, and 
colourful road markings. 
These improvements are 
designed to make the journey to 
school safer and more enjoyable 
for children and their families, 
while also encouraging walking, 
wheeling, and cycling.
At St Dominic’s National 
School, a new school zone on 
Mountain Park features raised 
zebra crossings—including one 
that improves access to St 
Dominic’s Shopping Centre—
SDCC Housing Capacity Review Underway
Officially opening of Airton 
Road Extension
The first revision of the National 
Planning Framework (NPF) was 
adopted by Government and 
both Houses of the Oireachtas 
in April this year. It updates 
Ireland’s national spatial 
planning and policy framework 
to 2040.
A key change is the revised 
population forecast of 5.8–6.1 
million by 2040, up from 5.15 
million in the 2022 Census. This 
brings a new national housing 
target of 50,000 homes per 
year—double the previous 
2018 target. This means that 
the Minister for Housing, Local 
Government and Heritage will 
shortly issue directions to all 
local authorities to review their 
County Development Plans to 
meet these updated targets.
In preparation for this, our 
Planning Department is 
reviewing all lands currently 
zoned for housing to assess 
capacity and deliverability. In 
parallel, the team will examine 
potential future development 
lands—those not yet zoned—
to identify the most suitable, 
sustainable, and deliverable 
options for potential rezoning.
This proactive approach, 
usually part of the statutory 
Development Plan review, is 
being brought forward to ensure 
readiness. If lands are identified 
for potential rezoning, they 
will be included in a public 
consultation process through 
a proposed variation to our 
County Development Plan, 
in line with the Planning and 
Development Act to ensure we 
plan responsibly for a growing 
and thriving future South 
Dublin.
Our outgoing Mayor, Cllr. 
Perrepadan, and Minister for 
Housing, local Government 
and Hertiage, James Browne, 
TD, officially opened the Airton 
Road Extension last month, 
marking a key milestone in 
our commitment to compact 
growth and better connectivity 
in Tallaght. 
Funded through the Urban 
Regeneration and Development 
Fund, the 330-metre single-
lane carriageway links Airton 
Road to Cookstown Road 
and includes active travel and 
district heating infrastructure, 
while also improving local 
access and unlocking for 
future mixed-use development 
supporting our regeneration 
and climate goals.

SDCC Meets Social 
Housing Targets
Affordable Homes: 
Canal Bank & Kilcarbery
Recently published data by 
the Department of Housing, 
local Government and Heritage 
on delivery of social housing 
by local authorities shows 
that SDCC successfully met 
our delivery target for 2022 
to 2024. Progress under our 
Housing Delivery Action Plan, 
a comprehensive strategy 
to increase housing delivery 
working together with Approved 
Housing Bodies and private 
sector partners, saw 1,825 
new social homes delivered 
in South Dublin, the second 
highest by any local authority 
and comprising 7.8% of all new 
social homes delivered. We 
also delivered 11.2% of all local 
authority own-build nationally. 
We continue to expand housing 
delivery to meet local needs 
and expect to reach our target 
of 772 new social homes this 
year, reflecting our proactive 
approach, strongly supported 
by our elected members and 
driven by the commitment of our 
housing delivery staff
Housing Loan Supports
The Local Authority Home 
Loan and the Purchase and 
Renovation Loan are available 
to support first-time buyers and 
fresh start applicants unable 
to secure funding from banks. 
These loans offer up to 90% of 
property market value and can 
be used for new or second-hand 
homes, including those under our 
affordable purchase scheme, while 
the Purchase and Renovation Loan 
also supports refurbishment of 
derelict or non-habitable homes 
eligible for the Vacant Property 
Refurbishment Grant. Please see 
www.localauthorityhomeloan.ie. 
for more information
Innovation Square: A New Chapter in Cost Rental Housing
Outgoing Mayor Cllr. Baby 
Perrepadan welcomed An 
Tánaiste, Simon Harris TD, and 
Minister for Housing, Local 
Government and Heritage, 
James Browne TD, to Tallaght 
last month to launch Innovation 
Square, our landmark cost 
rental development in the 
emerging Innovation Quarter. 
Innovation Square is part of 
a wider local masterplan that 
has seen delivery of new link 
roads, an innovation centre for 
business start-ups and high-
quality public realm for better 
connectivity and regeneration 
of the area under the Tallaght 
Local Area Plan. The 133 
apartment development is 
the largest single-tenure cost 
rental project to be delivered 
by a local authority in Ireland to 
date. It sets a new standard for 
how this housing model can be 
delivered, funded and managed 
and its central location offers 
excellent access to jobs, retail, 
education, public transport and 
local amenities.
With a project cost of €57 
million, the new development 
includes studio, one-and two-
bedroom apartments in podium 
blocks, along with interlinking 
three-bedroom homes and 
residents will benefit from a 
managed community facility, 
landscaped courtyard, bicycle 
and car parking. As the first cost 
rental scheme to be funded 
directly by a local authority, and 
supported by the government’s 
Affordable Housing Fund,  
monthly rents will be 25% below 
market rate, ranging from €950 
to €1,550, providing long-term, 
secure and more affordable 
homes. 
Please see sdcc.ie this month 
for details on how to register 
interest for these homes.
Over 580 applications have 
been submitted for 60 new 
affordable homes at Canal 
Bank, Clonburris which 
we launched for sale last 
month. These applications 
are being assessed under 
our Scheme of Priority for 
Affordable Dwelling Purchase 
Arrangements and successful 
applicants will shortly be 
contacted to progress their 
purchases. 
Our next launch of 70 
new affordable homes in 
Kilcarbery goes live on 17 July 
with one to four-bedroom 
homes available including 
houses, duplexes, and 
apartments. Prices start from 
€195k with details available 
on sdcc.ie, daft.ie and local 
and social media.

Developing Tallaght 
Stadium’s Future
DCU Access Programme
Following a competitive 
procurement process we are 
delighted to announce the 
appointment of Teneo Ireland 
to develop a new commercial 
strategy for Tallaght Stadium, 
including exploring the 
potential for new events and for 
securing enhanced sponsorship 
arrangements. 
This work aims is to strengthen 
the stadium’s brand and 
generate new revenue 
streams that will support 
ongoing investment in facility 
improvements that can further 
enhance the stadium’s role as a 
key asset for Tallaght and South 
Dublin. 
Elected members were recently 
briefed on the project at the 
Strategic Policy Committee, 
and the Council will be kept 
informed as the work progresses 
on delivering on our ambitions 
for the future of the stadium 
with the the process expected to 
be completed by the end of this 
year.
30 Years of Ace Enterprise 
Park Marked
ACE Enterprise Park marked its 
30th anniversary this month with 
a celebratory community garden 
party. The event brought together 
past and present members to 
reconnect and reflect on three 
decades of shared success. 
Founded in 1995, ACE has grown 
into a thriving, dual-campus social 
enterprise that now supports 
nearly 70 enterprises and over 250 
workers. ACE, supported by SDCC, 
has championed inclusion and 
local entrepreneurship to tackle 
unemployment, and continues 
to provide space and services to 
support local enterprises. 
Priory Market Puts Small Food Businesses on the Map in Tallaght
DCU Access Programme
The opening of Priory Market in 
Tallaght is welcomed by SDCC 
as a key milestone in delivering 
the County’s Food Strategy. 
The provision of an indoor food 
market has long been a core 
objective, supporting food 
innovation and creating new 
opportunities for local producers.
Officially opened on Wednesday, 
25 June, the €4 million market 
brings global flavours—from 
Venezuela to Korea—into the 
heart of the community. It offers 
rent-free units to a range of local 
small food businesses, with just 
15% of turnover going toward 
operating costs.
Funded through the now-closed 
Immigrant Investor Programme, 
€3.6 million was raised from 
nine investors, with an additional 
€400,000 from local social 
enterprise Partas. Designed with 
long-term sustainability in mind, 
the market reinvests profits into 
local jobs and training, hugely 
benefiting the local economy.
More than a food destination, 
Priory Market is now a platform 
for entrepreneurship, culture, and 
community. It supports inclusive 
economic growth and offers a 
scalable model for community-
led development.
The growth of the county’s food 
sector depends on collaboration 
between public and private 
partners. With the successful 
delivery of Priory Market by 
Partas, SDCC now looks ahead 
to progressing plans for a new 
dedicated food production hub 
in Tallaght, further strengthening 
the local food economy and 
supporting a thriving, sustainable 
sector.
SDCC is proud to support 
the DCU Access Programme 
for the first time in 2025 to 
assist students who may not 
otherwise access third-level 
education. A key feature is 
the Access to the Workplace 
module, offering a ten-week 
internship that builds skills, 
confidence, and real-world 
experience. 
Under the programme, one 
student is now working with 
our economic development 
team and we look forward 
to further developing this 
collaboration in the years 
ahead, reflecting our 
corporate commitment to 
creating greater opportunity 
for all in South Dublin.

Empowering Women at 
County Hall
Active Parks Returns
The council’s Women’s Caucus 
and LEO South Dublin’s NEWS 
network hosted an inspiring 
evening in County Hall on 
18 June. The event brought 
together women from across 
South Dublin to share stories, 
spark ideas, and support each 
other in work and life.
Chaired by Cllr. Vicki Casserly, 
the panel featured Flor Mac 
Carthy (Women for Election), 
international canoeist Jenny 
Egan-Simmons, Jennifer Philips 
(Women’s Collective Ireland), 
and entrepreneur Feebee 
Foran of Forager who offered 
advice and powerful insights 
on leadership, resilience, and 
community.
The event reflected our 
commitment to inclusive 
leadership and creating 
opportunities for all women 
to thrive, and was described 
as “vibrant, engaging, and full 
of energy,” by Cllr. Casserly 
who said “when women come 
together, they lift each other 
up and that has the power to 
change the world.”
Community Spirit at 
Mayors Awards
At the Mayor’s Awards on 25 June, 
SDCC celebrated the essence 
of local communities— our 
volunteers. Hosted by then Mayor 
Cllr. Baby Pereppadan in County 
Hall, the event honoured 14 
individuals and groups, from tidy 
towns, youth, sports and cultural 
groups who were nominated by 
councillors for their outstanding 
community spirit. 
“The measure of any place is the 
people that inhabit it,” said Cllr. 
Pereppadan, highlighting those 
who give their time and energy to 
enrich lives and make South Dublin 
a better place to live. 
Celebrating Refugee Week in South Dublin
Park Yoga returns with 
Active Parks 2025
Refugee Week, held from 16–22 
June, is the world’s largest arts 
and culture festival celebrating 
the creativity, resilience, and 
contributions of refugees and 
people seeking asylum. It is a 
time to come together, honour 
diverse cultures, and deepen our 
understanding of the journeys 
that bring people to Ireland.
To mark the occasion, our 
integration team hosted a 
vibrant programme of events 
across the county, designed to 
foster connection and celebrate 
inclusion.
On World Refugee Day, council 
staff were invited to a powerful 
Human Library event, where 
four colleagues courageously 
shared their personal stories 
of moving to Ireland. These 
lived experiences offered 
insight, empathy, and a deeper 
appreciation of the challenges 
and triumphs of resettlement.
The week culminated in a joyful 
community celebration at 
Dodder Valley Park. Families and 
neighbours gathered to enjoy 
live music, dance workshops, 
an art exhibition, and children’s 
activities including face painting 
and hair braiding. Attendees also 
sampled delicious food from 
around the world and joined in 
sports sessions led by Active 
South Dublin, with support from 
the Volunteer Centre.
It was a week of shared stories, 
new friendships, and cultural 
pride that highlighted the 
resilience and richness that 
diversity brings to South Dublin 
showing that together, we are 
building a more inclusive and 
connected community.
The Active Parks programme 
is back for 2025, bringing free 
outdoor fitness classes to 
communities across the county. 
This year’s line-up includes 
new locations—Corkagh Park, 
Tymon Park, and Jobstown 
Park—and new classes like 
Calisthenics, Pilates, and 
Zumba, alongside favourites 
such as Park Fit and Park Yoga.
Designed for all fitness levels 
(ages 16+), these sessions 
offer a fun, welcoming way 
to get active in the fresh air 
with classes for anyone trying 
something new or returning to a 
routine.
Find out more and book your 
free place at “Free Active Parks 
2025” on eventbrite.ie.

Knockmitten 3G Pitch 
Opens
Paint Re-use scheme
Last month saw the 
Knockmitten community 
and local sports groups 
welcome local area committee 
chairperson Cllr. Shirley 
O’Hara and other public 
representatives and council 
officials to officially open the 
new 3G pitch. 
Located beside Knockmitten 
Community Centre, the 
pitch along with a new 3v3 
basketball half-court and 
upgraded playspace, provides 
a vibrant and inclusive sports 
and play hub for a range of 
ages and abilities responded to 
locally identified priorities. 
Funded through the 
Department of Rural and 
Community Development’s 
Community Recognition 
Fund and from SDCC’s own 
resources, this project supports 
growing communities while 
also recognising the welcome 
extended by communities to 
new arrivals from Ukraine and 
other countries.
Protecting Our Environment
The Enivronmntal Protection 
Agency (EPA) recently reported 
that SDCC was one of only 
three local authorities that met 
the required standard of strong 
or excellent for all 19 national 
enforcement priorities for 2024. 
Over the year, we carried 
out 11,631 inspections and 
responded to 2,961 complaints 
demonstrating our commitment 
to protecting the environment. 
The EPA assessment performance 
in waste, water, air and noise 
enforcement with a rating of 
excellent standard awarded to us 
across seven areas.
New Playspace Opens at Saggart Community Centre
Rediscover paint at 
Ballymount Civic Amenity 
Paint Re-use scheme
The new playspace at Saggart 
Community Centre was officially 
opened by local area committee 
chairperson, Councillor Shirley 
O’Hara, alongside fellow elected 
representatives and members of 
the local community and council 
officials.
Situated beside the beautifully 
restored old schoolhouse, the new 
playspace brings fresh energy to 
this cherished community hub. 
The schoolhouse, now a vibrant 
centre for local activity, has been 
revitalised to serve local people 
of all ages and the addition of 
the playspace enhances this 
by creating a safe, welcoming 
environment where children 
can play freely and families can 
connect.
This development reflects 
SDCC’s ongoing commitment to 
building inclusive, active spaces 
that promote wellbeing and 
strengthen community ties. It 
also recognises the site’s heritage 
as a place of learning and play—
honouring the past while investing 
in the future.
The project was made possible 
through €380,000 in funding 
from the Department of Rural 
and Community Development’s 
Community Recognition 
Fund. This initiative supports 
communities that have opened 
their arms to new arrivals from 
Ukraine and beyond, recognising 
their generosity and resilience.
We are deeply grateful to the 
Saggart community, especially the 
dedicated staff and management 
of the community centre, whose 
collaboration and support helped 
bring this project to life, creating 
space that reflects and supports 
community and integration.
Last year, we launched a 
new partnership with the 
Rediscovery Centre to give 
unused, water-based paint a 
second life. Paint collected 
at Ballymount Civic Amenity 
is now sorted by trained 
staff and collected for reuse 
instead of disposal and the 
Rediscovery Centre then 
repurposes the paint to make 
it available at low cost to 
the public and community 
groups. 
Since its introduction, 
the innovative scheme 
has successfully diverted 
over one tonne of paint 
from landfill to support 
sustainability and better 
community access to 
affordable resources.

WorkIQ Turns One: 
WorkIQ Turns One: 
A Movement for Growth, Community, and South Dublin’s Future
A Movement for Growth, Community, and South Dublin’s Future
As WorkIQ reaches the 
milestone of its first 
anniversary, it is clear that 
something powerful is 
taking shape. What started 
as a flexible workspace for 
startups and innovation teams 
has grown into a thriving 
movement—one that is building 
momentum, creating high-
value jobs, and shaping the 
regions economic future from 
the ground up.
In just twelve months, over 
20 startups, scaleups, and 
innovation-led teams have 
made WorkIQ their base. 
These businesses span 
sectors from fintech and AI 
to sportstech, energy and 
the built environment. Each 
brings fresh energy, bold ideas, 
and a shared commitment to 
growth—not just for their own 
ventures, but for the wider 
business community. 
Companies like Decision 
Analytics, using data science 
to transform manufacturing, 
and TCC’s Career Navigator, 
opening up access to 
WorkIQ is now hosting over 20 startups
personalised career pathways, 
are laying the groundwork 
for more inclusive economic 
development. Surpass Sports 
and Eleva Marketing are doing 
more than delivering services—
they’re building strong local 
networks and enriching the 
area’s entrepreneurial spirit.
Flexidrive, fresh from closing 
its first major investment 
round, is changing how driving 
lessons are booked and 
managed. Epira AI is preparing 
to help government services 
embrace artificial intelligence. 
H3D is breaking new ground 
in healthtech, using AI to 
automate the design and fit 
of hearing aids, and Fortivum, 
a fast-growing consultancy, is 
expanding across Europe while 
staying rooted in Tallaght.
What connects them all is a 
belief that South Dublin is 
more than a place to start—it’s 
a place to belong.
Backed by SDCC and operated 
by Oxford Innovation Space, 
WorkIQ supports founders 
with the space, support, and 
community they need to thrive. 
Its hands-on business support 
is tailored to real challenges, 
helping early-stage companies 
move forward with confidence.
One year in, the momentum is 
real. Founders are supporting 
each other. New collaborations 
are forming. There’s a shared 
belief that the best kind of 
economic development is 
bottom-up and community-led.
As WorkIQ enters year two, one 
thing is clear: if you want to 
shape South Dublin’s future—
this is where you start.
Join the movement at www.
workiq.ie

The ongoing delivery of 
the Clonburris Strategic 
Development Zone (SDZ) is 
being led by SDCC through 
a unique partnership model 
involving both public and 
private stakeholders. 
Clonburris stands out for its 
delivery approach—a multi-
agency, plan-led model 
coordinated through Clonburris 
Infrastructure Limited, a 
special purpose vehicle and the 
first of its kind in Irish urban 
development.
The programme integrates over 
€205 million in public funding 
from the Urban Regeneration 
and Development Fund (URDF) 
and the National Transport 
Authority (NTA), along with 
local authority and private 
contributions. This enables 
the timely delivery of essential 
infrastructure including 
bridges, community facilities, 
roads, parks, and transport.
Infrastructure
The Clonburris infrastructure 
programme is structured into 
key delivery packages. The 
first, the Southern Link Street, 
is already partially open to 
the east, with full completion 
expected in early 2026.
Planning permission for the 
North Link Street was granted 
in February this year, with 
detailed design now underway 
and construction Construction 
is scheduled to begin in 2026.
The programme also includes 
the delivery of extensive green 
spaces and biodiversity-friendly 
public parks. A planning 
application covering Griffeen 
Valley Park, Na Cluainte Park 
South, and Canal Park South 
will be submitted this month.
Housing Delivery
At the heart of the Clonburris 
programme is delivery of 
homes alongside infrastructure. 
Progress to date includes:
•	
3,567 homes with planning 
permission
•	
Around 2,300 homes 
currently under 
construction
•	
685 homes completed and 
occupied
For updates and more 
information, visit sdcc.ie/
clonburris

A Clearer Structure for a 
Stronger Future
SDCC is stepping into a  
new chapter—one shaped  
by clarity, cohesion and a 
renewed commitment to  
the people we serve. 
As part of our new Corporate 
Plan, we’ve refreshed our 
organisational structure to 
better reflect our values and 
to deliver on our promise of 
opportunity for all. 
This is about making sure our 
structure supports the work 
we do and the people we do 
it for. That means refreshing 
directorates to better reflect 
today’s priorities while also 
simplifying directorate names 
so they are clearer and more 
meaningful to the public.  
We have also aligned work 
streams and departments that 
share a common purpose, so 
we can work more efficiently 
and deliver joined-up and 
people-focused services.
A dedicated Director of 
Housing reflects the scale and 
focus needed to deliver on 
our housing responsibilities. 
Another significant change 
sees a new Director of 
Community role to oversee 
the Community, Libraries and 
Corporate Services as well 
as our our public events and 
engagements—areas that 
represent our most visible and 
proactive engagements with 
the public. By uniting these 
areas, we’re strengthening 
our civic voice and raising the 
standard of how we connect 
with our communities. 
Other directorates have also 
been reimagined to better 
reflect today’s priorities. The 
Director of Climate Action 
now includes responsibility 
for active travel, while the 
Director of Planning and 
Transport will continue to 
guide the county’s growth and 
connectivity. 
The new Director of 
Digital Services will lead 
digitial transformation, 
cybersecurity, data protection 
and smart initiatives while 
the Director of Finance is 
now also responsible for 
procurement. The Director 
of Planning and Transport 
will guide connectivity and 
growth while the Director of 
Economic Development will 
lead enterprise and tourism 
functions and also manage 
Human Resources, recognising 
the importance of people 
leadership in shaping our 
future. 
These changes are supported 
by a new strategic workforce 
plan for the next five years 
that aims to grow our team 
and empower staff at every 
level. 
Our Senior Executive 
Officers will take on enhanced 
leadership roles in their areas, 
and new policies on mobility 
and succession planning 
will help everyone build a 
meaningful career here. This is 
about more than structure. It’s 
about building an organisation 
that’s fit for purpose, proud 
of its identity and ready to 
meet the needs of a growing, 
diverse county, together.
